scope: Verification of the deployed navigation-count fix. Same six HTTPS routes, one dedicated administrator, same resource budgets, flags and dispatch policy as the reference cohort.

method.clientProtocol: urllib HTTPS HTTP/1.1, new connection per request, gzip requested, no browser/network emulation
method.excludedWarmup: One initial traversal of six routes; no forced eviction or database page flush.
method.cacheFlags: New master and all layers off in both versions. Legacy caches retain a 60-second TTL.
method.guard: Pause new dispatch after five host-steal samples >=50 percent, resume after five below35; all response observations kept. Stop on observed OOM kill.
method.caveat: Different wall-clock windows on a shared VPS; CPU and background activity differ. Work reduction is validated separately with paired read-only queries. Latency changes are observational.
method.serverReportScope: HTTP log/pool aggregates start with the deployed container and include other traffic/health checks, without exact synthetic request correlation.

detailFollowUp: The five slowest captured project-detail events each spent 1519-3315 ms in detail.sources.labor with no observed pool queue peak. Source verification shows this calls the legacy 60-second labor-cost cache and monthly computation. CPU/network/GC contributions are not isolated; the client p95 remains slightly above the 1500 ms target.
limitations: One administrator, one selected project/group, light sequential traffic. No first-load p95, viewer/division/concurrency or production acceptance.
Read-only pairs measure only the employee-count subroutine in a serialized PostgreSQL transaction, not the whole navigation count endpoint.
Other fields of the count still require the allocation audit on first use or after invalidation; this work does not remove that calculation.

Dashboard hash comparison is reported explicitly. Its sources are unchanged and verified in the container; no prior full payload was retained for field-by-field attribution. Do not claim six-route cross-deployment financial parity.
Point recalculation and high CPU steal remain separate follow-up topics. No cache layer or existing service was reconfigured during the assessment.
Worker progress includes empty queue scans. One-off diagnostic Node processes execute in the API cgroup after the measured cohort; use the earlier cohort snapshot for memory observations.
Backups, retention and business records were not altered; authentication used normal disposable sessions and logout.

api.clientProtocol: urllib HTTPS HTTP/1.1, new connection per request, gzip requested, no browser/network emulation

publishedPairs.method: Published full pending view versus published employee-count method, five alternating pairs in one Repeatable Read / Read Only transaction. Serialized transaction queries; subroutine timings only.
